item.title: Nestle, Zydus, Abbott face India scrutiny over claims on children's products
item.description: India's food safety regulator issued notices to Nestle India , Zydus Wellness , Abbott Healthcare and others on Wednesday over promotional claims involving products for infants and children that it said breached rules.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's food safety regulator issued notices to Nestle India (NEST.NS) , Zydus Wellness (ZYDS.NS) , Abbott Healthcare and others on Wednesday over promotional claims involving products for infants and children that it said breached rules. The action comes days after the regulator [USN:L6N46302P TEXT:"proposed"] banning the addition of sucrose and fructose to foods for infants up to six months old, as India steps up scrutiny of food safety and pushes for front-of-pack warning labels, rattling the country's more than $100 billion packaged food industry. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India said it issued notices over products including Complan, Lactogen Pro 1 Powder, NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and infant milk substitutes. The regulator asked Nestle India to provide evidence supporting claims about digestive and immune-system benefits for its Lactogen Pro 1 Powder and NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 infant formula products. Nestle India said FSSAI's latest post reiterated issues raised on September 18 concerning product labels, and that it had already submitted a detailed response to the regulator. Zydus Wellness was asked to provide scientific justification for claims promoting its Complan children's drink, including the tagline "grow taller, faster. clinically proven 2X growth." The company did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours. FSSAI also issued notices to social media influencer Ira Fathima and companies including Abbott Healthcare and Nestle India over an Instagram reel promoting infant milk substitutes. An Abbott spokesperson said the company was not involved in or aware of the social media content referenced by the FSSAI notice and became aware of the content only after receiving the regulator's notice. "Abbott does not endorse the claims or representations contained in the content," the spokesperson said.

item.title: Europe's financial regulators query Google over cloud outage that hit banks
item.description: Financial regulators in Europe are questioning Google after a cloud computing outage on Tuesday left millions of bank customers without access to key financial services for hours.
item.dc:creator: Phoebe Seers, Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: Financial regulators in Europe are questioning Google after a cloud computing outage on Tuesday left millions of bank customers without access to key financial services for hours. The European Banking Authority said that it had been in contact with Google Cloud to obtain further information on the incident, understand its implications and assess its potential impact on financial entities in the EU, a spokesperson for the watchdog told Reuters. Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) said the disruption, [USN:L6N4660LB TEXT:"which lasted several hours,"] was caused by a "power event" in a London-based network that serves customers across Europe. Revolut, Lloyds (LLOY.L) and HSBC (HSBA.L) were among the banks affected. HSBC and Lloyds did not comment. A Google spokesperson said: "We have resolved a disruption to Google Cloud services at a third-party facility in our europe-west2 cloud region due to a power event. Services have been restored. We will update our public status dashboard with an analysis." At Revolut, which has around 13 million UK customers, a wide range of services including logging in, card payments and cash withdrawals were affected on Tuesday, according to the bank's website. Revolut said in a statement that it was reviewing the incident to reduce the impact of any future third-party disruptions, and that customer funds and data had remained safe throughout. The outage is the first major test of new rules across Europe designed to strengthen the resilience of technology providers, including cloud firms, on which the financial sector depends. The European Union last year designated 19 technology firms as critical third-party providers to the financial sector, bringing them under joint direct oversight of three financial regulators — including the EBA — for the first time. Britain took similar steps for four cloud providers, citing the risk that [USN:S8N41Y00R TEXT:"an outage at a major supplier could affect multiple financial firms"] at the same time. Google Cloud falls under both regulatory frameworks. "The designation of a provider as a Critical third-party provider establishes an EU-level oversight framework; it does not transfer responsibility for incident management from the provider or relieve financial entities of their own regulatory obligations," the EBA said in emailed comments. In Britain, parliament's Treasury Committee has written to the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), seeking details of the regulators' response to the outage on Tuesday, the scale of the disruption and any financial harm caused. The FCA said it was engaging with Google over the incident. Under Britain's critical third party regime, designated providers like Google Cloud must report serious outages to the FCA and the BoE. A spokesperson for the Bank of England declined to comment. Under EU and UK rules, banks are ultimately responsible for the services they provide to customers, including when they rely on third-party providers.

item.title: Activos en Brasil se mueven atentos a balotaje; peso mexicano cae con fuerza
item.description: Los activos brasileños cotizaron con bajas el miércoles, atentos a sondeos de intención de voto de cara al esperado y reñido balotaje presidencial del domingo, mientras que el peso mexicano fue golpeado por el desmantelamiento de posiciones de "carry trade", según analistas.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Los activos brasileños cotizaron con bajas el miércoles, atentos a sondeos de intención de voto de cara al esperado y reñido balotaje presidencial del domingo, mientras que el peso mexicano fue golpeado por el desmantelamiento de posiciones de "carry trade", según analistas. * Los mercados bursátiles de la región también reaccionaron a los reportes corporativos del tercer trimestre. * A nivel global, el dólar cayó ligeramente mientras los inversores ya comienzan a mirar de reojo la reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana. Los mercados descuentan que el banco central mantendrá los costos del crédito, pero esperan un endurecimiento monetario en diciembre. * Mientras, Wall Street avanzó en medio de resultados de firmas ligadas a la inteligencia artificial y el retorno de los bonos del Tesoro retrocedió. Los precios del petróleo cerraron con pocos cambios tras perder el impulso de más temprano cuando escalaron más de 2 dólares por barril. * El real brasileño cedió un 0,18% a 5,0272 por dólar, luego de tres sesiones de avances; al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) bajó preliminarmente un 0,92% a 206.379 puntos, al perder impulso tras superar las 209.000 unidades en la apertura después de conocerse un sondeo sobre el balotaje presidencial del domingo. * El Bovespa escaló más de un 1% en la ronda previa, con datos mostrando el ingreso de flujos de inversores extranjeros al mercado. * La ventaja del senador Flávio Bolsonaro sobre el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se ha reducido de cara a la segunda vuelta, reveló el miércoles una encuesta de Quaest. * El senador de derecha obtendría el 45% de los votos, frente al 44% del actual mandatario de izquierda. El sondeo anterior de Quaest, de hace una semana, mostró una ventaja de 46% a 44% en favor de Bolsonaro. * Las encuestas muestran que el senador mantiene una ventaja sobre el presidente de cara al balotaje, aunque la distancia se ha reducido y se estima que la elección será muy reñida. Bolsonaro ganó la primera vuelta pese a que la mayoría de los sondeos daban como triunfador a Lula. * El peso mexicano bajó un 1,4%, a 18,6714 unidades por dólar, un mínimo del año, afectado por la reducción del diferencial de tasas de interés con Estados Unidos. * El índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, trepó un 1,43%, a 70.249,54 puntos, en su quinta sesión de alzas consecutiva apuntalado por resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre. * "El peso mexicano es la divisa más depreciada en la sesión, debido a que continúa el desmantelamiento de posiciones de carry trade, ante la reducción del diferencial de tasas de interés entre México y Estados Unidos. Este diferencial se redujo a 250 puntos base desde el 16 de septiembre, cuando la Reserva Federal incrementó su tasa de interés en 25 puntos base", dijo Banco Base en un reporte. * Los mercados anticipan una nueva alza del costo del crédito en diciembre por parte de la Fed, mientras que en México no se descarta una reducción del costo del crédito durante el próximo año. * El peso colombiano cerró con caída de un 0,50% a 3.190 unidades por dólar, después de que el Gobierno anunció que fijará por decreto el presupuesto de gastos para 2027, luego de que el proyecto de ley aprobado por el Congreso se hundió por un vicio de trámite, generando incertidumbre sobre la distribución del gasto público en medio de persistentes presiones fiscales. * En la bolsa, el índice accionario COLCAP (.COLCAP) se valorizó un 1,08% a 2.560,52 puntos. * El peso chileno , cerró la jornada con una caída del 0,41%, en 978,20/978,50 unidades por dólar, en línea con sus pares de la región, mientras que el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , avanzó un 0,55%, a 10.987,14 puntos. * El peso mayorista argentino se depreció un leve 0,07% a 1.526 unidades por dólar, junto a contratos de futuros equilibrados e intervención del banco central (BCRA) para acumular reservas a favor de sus arcas. La entidad monetaria compró 46 millones de dólares del mercado cambiario. * Mientras, el índice líder MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires escaló un 1,68%, luego de acumular tres jornadas en baja. * La moneda peruana, el sol , finalizó con una caída de 0,23% a 3,4340/3,4350 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) retrocedió un 0,31% a 1.574,24 puntos.

item.title: Nasdaq lidera subida de Wall Street; resultados de SpaceX y Super Micro avivan interés por la IA
item.description: El Nasdaq, con gran presencia tecnológica, subió el miércoles después de que los resultados trimestrales de SpaceX y Super Micro Computer aumentaron el interés por las acciones relacionadas con la IA, pero la debilidad de los valores del sector de los servicios de comunicaciones limitó las ganancias.
item.dc:creator: Purvi Agarwal, Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: El Nasdaq, con gran presencia tecnológica, subió el miércoles después de que los resultados trimestrales de SpaceX y Super Micro Computer aumentaron el interés por las acciones relacionadas con la IA, pero la debilidad de los valores del sector de los servicios de comunicaciones limitó las ganancias. Las acciones de la empresa de cohetes y tecnología espacial de Elon Musk, SpaceX (SPCX.O) , se dispararon después de que el martes dijo que una fusión con Tesla (TSLA.O) sería "una buena idea". SpaceX también reportó sus primeras ganancias como empresa que cotiza en bolsa. Las acciones de Tesla avanzaban un 3,7%. Super Micro (SMCI.O) subió con fuerza y estuvo entre las acciones que más ganaron del S&P 500, después de que el fabricante de servidores de IA pronosticó unos ingresos trimestrales y un margen de ganancia superior a las estimaciones de Wall Street, lo que indica que la demanda se mantiene sólida. Los resultados de Super Micro impulsaron a algunos de sus competidores como HPE (HPE.N) y Dell (DELL.N) . Los reportes parecieron tranquilizar a los inversionistas, ya que la preocupación por la rentabilidad de la expansión de la IA desencadenó la semana pasada una ola de ventas en las acciones relacionadas con el sector, con el operador de centros de datos CoreWeave (CRWV.O) en el ojo del huracán. Las noticias de SpaceX "disipan algunas de las preocupaciones de los inversores" sobre la IA, junto con cierta ayuda del SMCI, según Angelo Kourkafas, estratega global sénior de Edward Jones. Kourkafas señaló que los informes no "responden a todas las preguntas que tienen los inversores sobre la rentabilidad de las inversiones en IA, pero es un buen comienzo". Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) subió 44,64 puntos, o un 0,58%, a 7.757,74 unidades, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganó 276,80 puntos, o un 1,05%, a 26.701,61. El Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) subió 355,90 puntos, o un 0,68%, a 52.851,78 unidades.

item.title: Dólar cae, operadores esperan reunión de la Fed la próxima semana
item.description: El dólar cayó el miércoles, mientras los operadores sopesaban los renovados riesgos de inflación impulsados por el petróleo y esperaban la reunión de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: El dólar cayó el miércoles, mientras los operadores sopesaban los renovados riesgos de inflación impulsados por el petróleo y esperaban la reunión de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana. * "En realidad, esta mañana no hay un tema dominante en los mercados y creo que seguirá siendo así al menos hasta la próxima semana, cuando se celebre la reunión del FOMC", dijo Shaun Osborne, estratega jefe de divisas de Scotiabank. "Tenemos que hacernos una idea de cuál es la postura de la Fed". * La guerra en curso entre Estados Unidos e Irán ha aumentado los temores a que la inflación impulsada por el petróleo pueda afectar a la política de la Fed. * Los precios del petróleo cerraron con escasos cambios, mientras los inversores sopesaban los posibles avances hacia unas negociaciones entre Rusia y Ucrania frente a la disminución de los inventarios de crudo en Estados Unidos y la ausencia de diálogo entre Washington y Teherán. * Los operadores de fondos de la Fed ven solo una pequeña posibilidad de que se produzca un alza de tasas la próxima semana, y se espera que la primera subida tenga lugar en diciembre. Tampoco es probable que el presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, dé pistas sobre futuros movimientos. * El dólar se debilitó la semana pasada a pesar de que los datos mostraron que la inflación de los precios al consumo en Estados Unidos se aceleró en septiembre. * A los inversores les preocupa cuánto tiempo puede durar el auge de las acciones relacionadas con la IA. El optimismo sobre el sector ha respaldado al dólar al atraer capital hacia Estados Unidos y elevar las expectativas de crecimiento e inflación. * El índice dólar , que mide la cotización de la moneda estadounidense frente a una cesta de seis divisas que incluye al yen y al euro, caía un 0,14% a 101,65 unidades, mientras que el euro subía un marginal 0,01% a 1,1237 dólares. * El euro se ha visto lastrado por las generalizadas protestas contra el Gobierno en Francia y por el deterioro de las perspectivas fiscales. El miércoles, los costos de financiación a 10 años de Francia alcanzaron máximos de 24 años. * La libra esterlina subía un 0,16% a 1,34 dólares a raíz de los datos que mostraron que la inflación del Reino Unido aumentó más de lo esperado el mes pasado, lo que reforzaba los argumentos a favor de una subida de tasas de interés por parte del Banco de Inglaterra en noviembre. Frente al euro, la libra alcanzó su nivel más alto en 17 meses. * El yen se apreciaba un 0,02%, a 158,12 unidades por dólar. El vicegobernador del Banco de Japón, Ryozo Himino, dijo que la inflación subyacente se situaba cerca del objetivo del 2% del banco central y que las condiciones financieras seguían siendo laxas, lo que apuntaba a un margen para un aumento de los costes de financiación.

item.title: Barril cierra estable mientras inversores analizan geopolítica y menores inventarios EEUU
item.description: Los precios del petróleo cerraron con escasos cambios el miércoles, mientras los inversores sopesaban los posibles avances hacia unas negociaciones entre Rusia y Ucrania frente a la disminución de los inventarios de crudo en Estados Unidos y la ausencia de diálogo entre Washington y Teherán.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo cerraron con escasos cambios el miércoles, mientras los inversores sopesaban los posibles avances hacia unas negociaciones entre Rusia y Ucrania frente a la disminución de los inventarios de crudo en Estados Unidos y la ausencia de diálogo entre Washington y Teherán. * Los futuros del crudo Brent ganaron 3 centavos, o un 0,03%, a 108,82 dólares por barril. Mientras, el crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate cedió 67 centavos, o un 0,68%, a 97,15 dólares. Ambos referenciales habían registrado alzas superiores a los 2 dólares durante la jornada; el Brent llegó a situarse cerca de sus niveles más altos en cinco meses. * En la sesión anterior, el Brent alcanzó su máximo en cinco meses, mientras que el WTI tocó su máximo en seis meses, antes de que los precios retrocedieran a raíz de las conversaciones sobre los esfuerzos de mediación en una reunión entre el presidente de Irán y el jefe del ejército de Pakistán en Teherán. * El Kremlin informó que el presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, aceptó reanudar las conversaciones de paz con Ucrania, con mediación estadounidense, a partir del próximo mes. El acuerdo se produjo tras una reunión entre Putin y el enviado de Estados Unidos Steve Witkoff, en el marco de los esfuerzos más recientes de Washington por poner fin al conflicto más sangriento en Europa desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial. * El miércoles, el ministro de Exteriores de Irán, Abbas Araqchi, dijo al Financial Times que Irán estaba preparado para defenderse, y el presidente Masoud Pezeshkian afirmó a medios estatales que Estados Unidos no podía esperar un diálogo mientras mantuviera el bloqueo y amenazara a Irán. * Según datos de Kpler, se registraron al menos 18 ataques a buques en las últimas dos semanas, mientras que los analistas de LSEG advirtieron que Irán estaba atacando petroleros mucho más allá del estrecho de Ormuz, llegando hasta el golfo de Omán y poniendo en peligro las cargas de crudo del Golfo y los trasvases de barco a barco que dan soporte a las operaciones de carga regionales. * El Departamento de Energía de Estados Unidos informó el miércoles que el Gobierno ofrece prestar hasta casi un tercio de su reserva de emergencia de combustible para calefacción, que asciende a un millón de barriles, con el fin de contener los precios, los cuales se han disparado debido a la escasez de diésel provocada por los conflictos en Irán y Ucrania. * La Administración de Información de Energía (EIA) de Estados Unidos comunicó el miércoles que las existencias de crudo en el país disminuyeron la semana pasada en 3,06 millones de barriles, a 412,5 millones de barriles, frente a la previsión de analistas consultados por Reuters que esperaban una reducción de 820.000 barriles.

item.title: US congressional candidate Brad Lander released after being detained by Israeli military in West Bank
item.description: Brad Lander, a US Democratic Party candidate for Congress, was detained by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, along with other Americans and Israelis harvesting olives alongside Palestinian farmers, rights groups said.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: Brad Lander, a US Democratic Party candidate for Congress, was detained by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, along with other Americans and Israelis harvesting olives alongside Palestinian farmers, rights groups said. Lander wrote on X that he had been released with a warning, which he said was apparently due to his public profile, but said several dozen rabbis and other participants were still detained. "The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn't a crime under any law I know," he earlier posted, saying he had been detained by the military. Lander, who is Jewish, was among a group of international volunteers, which one organiser said also included British and Canadian citizens, accompanying local Palestinian farmers as an act of solidarity in what is known as protective presence. The farmers often face the threat of violence from Israeli settlers. Lander is a former New York City comptroller and mayoral candidate who is running for New York's 10th Congressional District in the US House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections . He is an ally of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and is critical of Israel's conduct in the war in Gaza . The annual olive harvest is a cultural tradition and important source of income for Palestinians. It is also often the target of violent attacks carried out by Israeli militant settlers. Israeli settler attacks against Palestinians and other civilians in the West Bank over the weekend prompted a call by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government to [USN:SPN45V01F TEXT:"crack down"] on the violence. "The story here is how hard the Israeli government works to make it impossible for Palestinian farmers to harvest their olive groves and drive on their roads and live in their homes and stay on their land," Lander said in a call with reporters from Beit Jala in the West Bank. "And I've had a chance to see that with my own eyes." Lander said he was detained for about three hours, including the time spent being held at the harvest, while the others he was with were detained for about nine hours. Israel's foreign ministry accused Lander of "looking for a confrontation" and said that he had ignored advice ahead of his visit that coordination with Israeli authorities was required. In response, Lander said the Israeli embassy in DC had recommended coordination with local authorities but did not explicitly say it was necessary. He also said he had taken part in olive harvesting the previous two days without incident. The incident took place in Nahalin, a village south of Bethlehem, as Palestinians were gathering olives accompanied by around 80 volunteers, according to Israeli organisation Rabbis for Human Rights and Jewish North American organisation T'ruah. Israeli police said it had detained Palestinian olive harvesters and dozens of Israeli and foreign activists gathering olives near the fence of an Israeli settlement, saying it was prohibited. One of the foreign nationals was later released once it became known he was a congressional candidate, police said. 'HARVESTING OLIVES IS NOT ILLEGAL' The military said harvesting in that area, which is located near the Israeli settlement of Beitar Illit, required prior coordination, which had not happened, and that those present had been detained. It did not say harvesting there was prohibited but that the "uncoordinated harvest" posed a security risk. "We did not present a security risk to anyone. We did nothing more provocative than harvest olives," Lander said. Mamdani wrote on X that Lander was among New Yorkers, including rabbis, who had been detained by Israel's government for accompanying Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest. "Harvesting olives is not illegal. The occupation is," he said, accusing Israel of genocide, and demanding the release of the other New Yorkers and an end to the Israeli occupation. Israel's government has denied accusations, including by a UN commission, and international and Israeli rights groups, that it is committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Police later said 72 people had been released, some on condition that they stay away from the harvest area. It also said four foreign nationals would face a hearing on Thursday to determine whether they would be deported. Rabbis for Human Rights and T'ruah said Israeli military and police forces arrived around two hours after the Palestinians and volunteers began gathering olives, and informed them that they were in a closed military zone. The participants were not aware it was a closed military zone and offered to leave, Rabbis for Human Rights Acting Director Anton Goodman had told Reuters by phone from the Beitar Illit police station, where he was being detained. Israeli forces, however, said they were detaining the participants, who Goodman said accused them of disturbing the public before taking them to the police station. T'ruah Chief Executive Rabbi Jill Jacobs, who was among those detained, said that before the Israeli forces arrived the volunteers had been picking olives with the Palestinian farmers "very peacefully". "We were obviously not doing anything violent but just the very act of picking olives together with Palestinian farmers was apparently disturbing for some," said Jacobs, a 51-year-old rabbi from Manhattan, in a phone interview. A spokesperson for the US Embassy in Jerusalem said it was aware of reports that US citizens had been detained.

item.title: Nasdaq leads Wall Street gains as SpaceX, Super Micro boost AI sentiment
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related stocks while weakness in communication services stocks capped gains.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: The tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related stocks while weakness in communication services stocks capped gains. SpaceX shares (SPCX.O) finished up 7.8% after Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm posted its first profit as a public company. Musk said, following the report, that [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"a merger of SpaceX"] and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea," also boosting Tesla shares. Elsewhere in earnings, Super Micro (SMCI.O) shares jumped 9.6% and it was among the S&P 500's top gainers after the AI server maker [USN:L4N4661QH TEXT:"forecast"] quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. The report also benefited peers HPE (HPE.N) , which rose 3.7%, and Dell (DELL.N) , which rose 5.3%. The reports provided some reassurance to investors who have been worried about the sustainability of massive spending on AI buildouts and their profitability. The technology sector was hammered last week by a selloff in AI-linked stocks, with data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) at the center of the storm. The SpaceX news "pushes back on some of the investor worries" about AI along with some help from Super Micro, according to Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones. Kourkafas said the reports will not "answer all the questions investors have on returns on AI investments, but it's a good start." As a result, the S&P 500 Information Technology index (.SPLRCT) finished up 1.6%, the biggest gainer among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors. "It's really a positive technology story for almost anyone that is somewhat involved in the artificial intelligence ecosystem," said Marc Dizard, chief investment officer at Huntington Bank. "The technology market reaction has been a reaffirmation that the artificial intelligence trade is still intact," he added. However, Dizard said sentiment can quickly shift around AI and that investors will seek reaffirmation when they monitor earnings reports from other companies. Shares in [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"Meta"] (META.O) rose 3% in late trading after it released its quarterly results following the regular session's close. After finishing up 3.4% in the regular session, [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"Tesla"] shares rose another 1.6% following its report, which was also issued after the close. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 360.21 points, or 0.69%, to 52,856.09, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 44.60 points, or 0.58%, to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 278.04 points, or 1.05%, to 26,702.86. Within technology, one of the strongest areas was chips with a 2% rally in the Philadelphia Semiconductor index (.SOX) , which has had a volatile month so far including an eight-session selloff. Gains in the benchmark S&P 500 were limited however by a 1.3% decline in communication services stocks (.SPLRCL) . The biggest losers included telecom operators such as AT&T (T.N) , which sank 6.5% even as it beat [USN:L4N4670UN TEXT:"third-quarter"] revenue and profit expectations. The SpaceX results, along with a recent wireless spectrum purchase, fanned fears that it could become a formidable competitor in telecoms, according to Dizard. T-Mobile US (TMUS.O) shares fell 2.5% and Verizon Communications (VZ.N) lost 2.2%. Also in communications services, Netflix (NFLX.O) shares sank 5.3% after the video streaming company issued [USN:L6N4661BU TEXT:"a weaker-than-expected forecast"] for its fourth-quarter profit. Google's parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) also declined 1.6%. Abbott Laboratories (ABT.N) shares dropped 1.9% after the medical device maker cut its [USN:L4N4670ZJ TEXT:"2026 sales growth forecast"]. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.37-to-1 ratio on the NYSE where there were 131 new highs and 221 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 2,690 stocks rose and 2,068 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.3-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 26 new 52-week highs and 3 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 53 new highs and 216 new lows. On US exchanges roughly 16.11 billion shares changed hands compared with the 17.10 billion average for the last 20 sessions.

item.title: TSX hits four-week high as investors cheer government support measures
item.description: Canada's main stock index rose to a four-week high on Wednesday, led by gains for financial shares, as investors welcomed government measures to aid sectors hit hard by US tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rose to a four-week high on Wednesday, led by gains for financial shares, as investors welcomed government measures to aid sectors hit hard by US tariffs. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 217.03 points, or 0.6%, at 36,324.99, its highest closing level since September 22. Canada and the province of Ontario unveiled a C$9 billion ($6.4 billion) [USN:L1N4670YW TEXT:"support package"] to help the steel and auto sectors deal with US tariffs and also boost critical mineral support chains. "Investors are really focused on the major projects, the government support, some tax changes that will help corporate investment and this is all very bullish for the Canadian stock market," said Lorne Steinberg, president, Lorne Steinberg Wealth Management Inc. Last month, Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Canada will let businesses [USN:L1N4570FS TEXT:"immediately write off"] the cost of most new capital investments for tax purposes. "The banks are going to be huge beneficiaries," Steinberg said. "They'll be lending to all of those projects." Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) rose 1.4%, with shares of Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD.TO) ending nearly 2% higher. Technology (.SPTTTK) added 0.8%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq led gains on [USN:L6N46710V TEXT:"Wall Street"] as quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improving appetite for AI-linked stocks. Industrials (.GSPTTIN) rose 0.7% and interest rate sensitive utilities (.GSPTTUT) were up 0.6%. The Canadian 10-year yield eased 2.3 basis points to 3.870%. Just three of the 10 major sectors ended lower, including consumer discretionary (.GSPTTCD) , which lost 1.4%. Auto parts supplier Magna International (MG.TO) was down 4.1% as CIBC and BNP Paribas cut their price targets on the stock. [USN:L4N4671NC TEXT:"Teck Resources"] (TECKb.TO) said it received strike notice from United Steelworkers Local 7619 at its Highland Valley Copper operations in British Columbia. The company's shares ended 2.6% lower.

item.title: Trump to tout crackdown on overseas crypto scams
item.description: President Donald Trump will highlight his administration's efforts on Wednesday to crack down on foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent crypto investments, a White House official told Reuters, as part of a broader event about cyber crime prevention.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump will highlight his administration's efforts on Wednesday to crack down on foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent crypto investments, a White House official told Reuters, as part of a broader event about cyber crime prevention. Speaking at a White House event, Trump and members of his cabinet are expected to highlight the government's seizure of fraudulent crypto investment websites and efforts to stop online impersonation scams, the official said. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FBI Director Kash Patel, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Attorney General Todd Blanche are expected to attend, the official added. White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross are also expected to be there, according to an administration official. Americans filed more than a million complaints with the FBI about internet scams last year, a 17% increase from 2024, according to an agency report, which also noted that Americans who filed complaints reported the highest losses. Trump's family is heavily involved in soliciting investments in crypto . A Reuters investigation found the Republican president and his sons have added at least $2.3 billion to the family fortune from their main crypto ventures, while the investors they have wooed have taken a $2.3 billion hit. White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly in a statement to Reuters about its investigation said, "All actions by President Trump and his administration are taken in the best interest of the American people." Trump in October 2025 [USN:FWN3W42W4 TEXT:"pardoned"] Changpeng Zhao, the convicted founder of the Binance cryptocurrency exchange. Zhao quit his job after the [USN:L1N3CM1MQ TEXT:"company"] pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program. In a March executive order, Trump directed the Justice Department to prioritize identifying and prosecuting scammers who carry out crimes online. Trump later directed the Department of Homeland Security to [USN:FWN4491P7 TEXT:"work"] with private companies to surveil foreign criminal hacking groups.

item.title: Booking.com targeted in EU investigation into phishing scams, fraudulent listings
item.description: EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: EU tech regulators will investigate whether online hotel reservation website Booking.com is doing enough to weed out fraudulent listings and phishing scams to comply with EU online content rules, the European Commission said on Wednesday. The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition enforcer, said it opened an investigation following a preliminary probe and after analysing risk assessment reports submitted by Booking.com this year and the previous three years. Big online platforms are required to do more to tackle illegal and harmful content on their sites under the bloc's Digital Services Act, or risk fines of as much as 6% of their global annual turnover for violations. Booking.com said it was engaging constructively with the Commission. "Security, trust and the protection of personal information are top priorities at Booking.com," a spokesperson for the company said. "We remain committed to working with relevant governments, regulators, law enforcement and industry partners to combat cybercrime and online fraud, and protect travelers and partners." The EU investigation will focus on fake listings — such as for non-existent properties — impersonation fraud and non-compliant accommodation offers, and whether Booking.com has properly identified, assessed and mitigated the systemic risks related to these. Regulators will also look into phishing scams exploiting Booking.com's reservation and guest data shared with accommodation providers, the Commission said. A third element will be paid-for boosted listings not clearly identifiable as advertisements. Booking.com is part of Booking Holdings (BKNG.O) . "Europeans should be able to book their holidays without fear of being scammed," EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said in a statement. "The Digital Services Act sets clear responsibilities on platforms to address these risks, and we must ensure that the leading booking platform in Europe takes those responsibilities seriously," she said.

item.title: For Flavio Bolsonaro, runoff vote tests Brazilians' appetite for family's political brand
item.description: For right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, his biggest strength is also his greatest weakness: the Bolsonaro family name.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: For right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, his biggest strength is also his greatest weakness: the Bolsonaro family name. While supporters across Brazil consider him a more moderate iteration of his father's powerful conservative brand, many others view him as a continuation of Jair Bolsonaro's scorched-earth rule that polarized the nation and culminated in an [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"attempted coup"] after he lost the 2022 election. So far, more voters seem willing to test the first hypothesis, with Bolsonaro heading into Sunday's run-off as the [USN:S8N442025 TEXT:"frontrunner"] against incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. A Bolsonaro victory would shift Brazil sharply rightward after four years of leftist rule, and likely push Latin America's largest nation closer into the orbit of the United States led by President [USN:S0N3ZY04Q TEXT:"Donald Trump"]. DISSATISFACTION WITH LULA Flavio's unexpected candidacy caught both insiders and markets off guard, especially since lingering corruption allegations — which he denies — and a crowded conservative field appeared to complicate his path to the presidency. But analysts say he has capitalized on growing [USN:L2N3QG01R TEXT:"dissatisfaction"] with 80-year-old Lula, while also tapping into his father's conservative coalition of powerful farmers, big business and evangelicals. Flavio, who is himself a converted evangelical, says that running for president felt like a calling after his father was sentenced to 27 years in prison for coup-plotting, a sentence he is now serving under house arrest. "I understand that everything happening is God's plan for our nation," [USN:L6N3XR02X TEXT:"he told Reuters"] late last year just after announcing his bid with his father's blessing. Murilo Miranda, a 42-year-old physician who attended a recent Bolsonaro rally in Sao Paulo, said Lula had overseen a system of welfare handouts and a bulging bureaucracy that had hindered Brazilian growth and led to endemic corruption. "They think the state is a father figure that is going to save them," Miranda told Reuters. Hermano Silveira, a 51-year-old contractor who was also at the rally, said Flavio was a new political force. "He is a young guy and we want change," Silveira said. RESOLVE HIS FATHER'S LEGAL PROBLEMS Bolsonaro has sought to acknowledge his father's missteps in power while tapping into his fervent base. During the first debate with Lula, he recognized his father's mishandled COVID-19 response, seeking to address a frequent line of attack. "Healthcare was not an area in which we achieved our best results under President Bolsonaro," he said. "I make this mea culpa here today." However, Bolsonaro has been clear that if he wins, he will quickly resolve his father's legal troubles. "I ask God for the opportunity to walk up the ramp of Planalto Palace next year alongside President Jair Messias Bolsonaro, so that he may place the presidential sash across my chest," he said on the campaign trail. So far, Bolsonaro has announced only one cabinet choice, naming Claudio Lottenberg, the former head of the private Albert Einstein hospital, as his pick for health minister. While promising to [USN:L1N4610Z9 TEXT:"cut spending"], Flavio has also pledged to boost public services and protect social welfare benefits for the population.

item.title: Shark nicknamed 'Bukangi' returns to sea off South Korea after third rescue attempt
item.description: A shark that became a sensation after spending more than a month in a canal in the South Korean port of Busan was successfully guided back into the open sea on Wednesday, following two failed rescue attempts, the oceans ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Hyun Yi, Daewoung Kim
item.content:encoded: A shark that became a sensation after spending more than a month in a canal in the South Korean port of Busan was successfully guided back into the open sea on Wednesday, following two failed rescue attempts, the oceans ministry said. The shark, nicknamed "Bukangi", was first spotted in a narrow waterway on September 18. More than 1.6 million people visited the waterfront park through October 20 to catch a glimpse of it, according to the Busan Infrastructure Corporation. Lee Min-jeung, a 39-year-old travel content creator from Seoul, said she had travelled to Busan four times to see Bukangi. "I'm relieved that it seems to have returned to the sea," Lee said. "Goodbye. Don't get sick." South Korea's National Institute of Fisheries Science identified Bukangi as a female dusky shark measuring about 3 meters (10 feet) in length. WARMING WATERS COULD BE BEHIND SIGHTINGS The species, which inhabits tropical, subtropical and temperate waters, is classified as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. Bukangi's appearance has also drawn attention to changes in the waters around South Korea, with experts citing warming seas as one possible factor behind a rise in large shark sightings. The fisheries institute recorded 46 sightings of large sharks along the country's east coast in the first half of this year, compared with 12 during the same period last year. The shark's stay was unusual because the narrow canal lies near high-rise buildings and a major high-speed rail station in central Busan. The operation to free it was deemed necessary because the shark had not been observed feeding, and falling temperatures could affect its health, city officials said. South Korean media also said Bukangi had sustained minor injuries to its fin and snout. Authorities tried to guide it out on September 29 and October 2 but both attempts were unsuccessful. On Wednesday, authorities used a net attached to floating platforms and divers to navigate the canal's underwater terrain and varying depths. Workers moved the net toward the sea while preventing the shark from swimming back into the canal.
